item.title: Apalachee High School shooting suspect pleads guilty to all charges
item.description: Colt Gray was charged with 55 counts, including malice murder, and faces life in prison without parole for the deadly mass shooting at Apalachee High School.

item.title: Trump says "nobody got out ahead" of him on Saudi nuclear deal announcement after changing terms
item.description: President Trump took questions from reporters the day after he seemed to upend a nuclear agreement with Saudi Arabia by adding a new condition: that the country join the Abraham Accords. CBS News White House reporter Olivia Rinaldi has the details.

item.title: Canada's Doug Ford on why country needs to "fight back" against Trump trade war
item.description: "We didn't start this war," Ontario Premier Doug Ford told CBS News on "The Takeout."

item.title: Costa Rica captures top fugitive "Diablo," wanted by U.S., officials say
item.description: Alejandro Arias-Monge, 41, had a $500,000 U.S. bounty on his head for alleged drug trafficking.

item.title: Tony Romo arrested in Wisconsin on suspicion of driving while intoxicated
item.description: The Milwaukee County Sheriff's Office said Romo was pulled over around 6 p.m. on Thursday.

item.title: Iran keeps targeting American bases as U.S. interceptor stockpiles dwindle
item.description: Explosions were heard near a U.S. base in Iraq, and Iran said it targeted Bahrain, Jordan and Kuwait as the 21-week war intensifies.

item.title: Ontario Premier Doug Ford says "we didn't start this trade war" as Trump slaps Canada with tariffs
item.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford spoke with CBS News senior White House and political correspondent Ed O'Keefe about the upcoming opening of the Gordie Howe Bridge and President Trump's new tariffs on Canada. "We didn't start this trade war. President Trump decided to go after his close ally and friend, his number one customer in the entire world," Ford said.

item.title: South Carolina on cusp of being first 2028 Democratic presidential primary state
item.description: The DNC Rules and Bylaws Committee voted Friday to recommend that South Carolina should hold the nation's first 2028 presidential nominating contest.

item.title: Sen. Peters wants to know why ICE bought spyware that can take control of phones
item.description: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement has purchased commercial spyware that can covertly take control of phones, collect messages, photos and location information.

item.title: All 11 on seaplane that crashed, caught fire north of Seattle survive
item.description: A seaplane with 11 people on board crashed and caught fire a short time later in the Puget Sound area north of Seattle. All 11 survived, authorities said.

item.title: Trump says U.S. to investigate EU trade practices over tech company fines
item.description: President Trump accused the European Union of "robbing" American companies and taxpayers.

item.title: LeBron James heading to Philly in deal with 76ers
item.description: The Sixers' wild offseason continued Friday when they added four-time NBA champion LeBron James.

item.title: How Trump's new round of tariffs could impact businesses and consumers
item.description: The markets showed a muted reaction as President Trump announced the latest round of tariffs on Thursday over "forced labor" concerns. Moneywatch correspondent Kelly O'Grady reports.

item.title: Trump to meet with Zelenskyy amid pressure for military support against Russia
item.description: President Trump is set to meet with Ukrainian President Zelenskyy on Tuesday amid calls for military support against Russia as Ukraine gains ground in the conflict. The Trump administration also recently imposed a new round of tariffs on dozens of countries, alleging forced labor concerns. Nicole Killion breaks it down.

item.title: Here is how cyclospora outbreak is affecting businesses
item.description: Visits to fast casual restaurants with lettuce-heavy menus are seeing declining foot traffic in the wake of the cyclosporiasis outbreak.

item.title: FDA panel recommends loosening regulations for some peptides
item.description: The FDA panel is reviewing seven peptides and deciding if they should be added to a list of substances that can be safely produced by compounding pharmacies.

item.title: DOJ withdraws subpoenas for New York Times reporters over Air Force One story
item.description: The Justice Department withdrew its subpoenas for New York Times reporters during a court heraing Thursday, after a judge grilled government lawyers for making "errors."

item.title: DOJ admits legal errors, drops subpoenas of New York Times journalists
item.description: A judge criticized the Justice Department for legal errors that ultimately led the agency to withdraw its subpoenas of two New York Times journalists who wrote a story about security concerns on President Trump's Qatari-gifted Air Force One. CBS News' Katrina Kaufman has the latest.

item.title: Moms speak out, alleging their sons were switched at birth decades ago
item.description: The mothers of two men who accuse a North Dakota hospital of switching them at birth are speaking out after the discovery.

item.description: The Secret Service says there has been a significant rise in threats ahead of the rescheduled White House Correspondents' Dinner. CBS News' Nicole Sganga has more details.

item.title: How Trump's threat of a "massive attack" on Iran could unfold
item.description: President Trump said he is considering a "massive attack" on Iran as fighting ramps up. CBS News' Charlie D'Agata explains how a U.S. military attack on Iran could unfold.

item.title: Trump expected to attend White House Correspondents' Dinner redo after April attack
item.description: President Trump is expected to attend the redo of the White House Correspondents' Dinner on Friday night after an armed assailant upended April's dinner.

item.title: Democrats' 2028 presidential primary schedule discussion exposes party divisions
item.description: Democrats are meeting to decide their 2028 presidential primary schedule. Their choices will set the stage for which candidates get an early lead in the race. CBS News political reporter Zak Hudak has more.

item.title: Pentagon website "anomalies" that removed names of 4 killed in Iran war remain
item.description: The Pentagon website, which was last updated on July 22, still showed only 14 killed in the conflict as of Friday.

item.title: White House Correspondents' Dinner rescheduled for July 24
